name: Fuel economy conversion
seoDesc: Fuel economy conversion: work out liters per 100 kilometers from the miles per US gallon. A free conversion calculator with the formula, units and a…
summary: The Fuel economy conversion calculator returns liters per 100 kilometers from the field on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. That makes it useful for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Fuel economy conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The Fuel economy conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports liters per 100 kilometers in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the miles per US gallon.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html: • A measured quantity, entered by default in miles per gallon (US). The unit chip switches it to any of the 10 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Fuel economy conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Liters per 100 kilometers=miles per US gallon
Miles per UK gallon=liters per 100 kilometers
Kilometers per liter=liters per 100 kilometers

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in liters per 100 kilometers, and convertible to any of the 10 units on that chip.
  • Shown in miles per gallon (UK), and convertible to any of the 10 units on that chip.
  • Shown in kilometers per liter, and convertible to any of the 10 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Fuel economy, opening in miles per gallon (US)
  • Fuel economy, opening in miles per gallon (UK)
  • Fuel economy, opening in liters per 100 kilometers
  • Fuel economy, opening in kilometers per liter

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Fuel economy conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Converting a figure someone quoted you so you can compare it
  • Reading a recipe written in units you do not use
  • Checking a product listing against the measurements you work with
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the miles per US gallon — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Fuel economy conversion calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Fuel economy conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns liters per 100 kilometers, derived from the miles per US gallon. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Fuel economy conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the miles per US gallon, which is 1 field in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter miles per US gallon in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Miles per US gallon opens in miles per gallon (US) and the chip beside it offers 10 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Fuel economy conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
